pages.title: Asyra Framework
pages.description: Build app-owned Features without rebuilding transaction, validation, lifecycle, persistence, or projection infrastructure.

pages.title: Create a complete design app
pages.description: Begin with the maintained Asyra Design product template and extend it as an app owner.

pages.title: Extend Asyra with an AI coding agent
pages.description: Give an AI agent bounded ownership, canonical APIs, and executable proof while you retain product decisions.

pages.title: Compose the official 2D baseline
pages.description: Apply the optional official Preset before Core starts, then keep app-domain choices outside the Framework.

pages.title: Compose only the infrastructure you need
pages.description: Start from Core and choose information, interaction, rendering, persistence, collaboration, and AI capabilities independently.

pages.title: Information models come before output
pages.description: Define app-owned information and rules without forcing it to be visible, rendered, collaborative, or AI-operated.

pages.title: Intent enters through Features
pages.description: Translate user or agent intent into explicit Feature sessions rather than mutating owners from UI or transport code.

pages.title: Give every state one canonical owner
pages.description: Separate canonical model state, local derived state, projection state, and remote transport state.

pages.title: One user intent, one transaction
pages.description: Commit, roll back, undo, redo, publish, and persist one intended action through one canonical boundary.

pages.title: Validate at every write and load boundary
pages.description: Keep schema validation in the Framework while version interpretation and migration remain app-domain responsibilities.

pages.title: Register projections; replace providers
pages.description: Keep canonical information independent from render layers and engine providers so output can be extended or replaced.

pages.title: Current runtime and future Core Kernel
pages.description: Distinguish today's browser/Core composition from the researched Headless and Core Kernel direction for machine-facing products.

pages.title: Build a custom component and schema
pages.description: Register app-owned component meaning, property defaults, and validation through public Core APIs.

pages.title: Build a transaction-safe Feature session
pages.description: Map start, update, end, and cancellation to exactly one intended undo commit.

pages.title: Build a custom render boundary
pages.description: Provide an engine through the public provider contract without teaching Core a renderer-specific implementation.

pages.title: Build hierarchy and Group behavior
pages.description: Keep parent-child ordering canonical while group meaning and geometry policy remain app-owned.

pages.title: Build persistence with app-owned migration
pages.description: Load validated canonical state while the app owns document versions, migration rules, and unsupported-version policy.

pages.title: Build opt-in collaboration
pages.description: Connect deterministic collaboration actors while the app owns transport, authorization, presence, and backend policy.

pages.title: Build registered AI actions
pages.description: Expose bounded action schemas and permissions so AI intent uses the same canonical transaction paths as people.

pages.title: Build app-owned AI retrieval and action
pages.description: Let the app retrieve domain context and register actions without presenting future Headless support as current behavior.
